# Workflows from earlier work in this repository

Reusable steps learned from earlier tasks here. Values your task states are filled in; blanks in braces stand for the rest of your task's own names and values. Places are found in the code as it is now (current line numbers); the lines shown are excerpts.

## 1. Document a new rule (doc, README, CHANGELOG)
Filled from your task: {rule_alias} = `no-duplicate-heading`, {tag} = `# Install`
Blanks: {rule_id} rule identifier such as MDnnn; {rule_file} lower-case rule id used as file name; {rule_description} the rule's description; {param} parameter name(s)
1. Create `doc-build/{rule_file}.md` with the prose body of the rule doc (what triggers it with a markdown example, default behaviour, rationale, how to fix). Copy the style of an existing doc-build file.
   a new file in `doc-build/`, named like the 57 there that start with ``; shortest first: heading.md (6 lines), footing.md (8 lines), md039.md (14 lines), md018.md (20 lines), md061.md (20 lines), md019.md (21 lines)
2. Add a CHANGELOG entry for the new rule ({rule_id}/no-duplicate-heading) as a bullet in the topmost, not-yet-released section at the top of the file (create that section heading if the top section is already a released version).
3. Add the rule bullet `- **[{rule_id}](doc/{rule_file}.md)** *no-duplicate-heading* - {rule_description}` to the rule list in README.md.
4. In README.md, find the bullet for the # Install tag in the tag list (it lists the rule ids of that tag) and add {rule_id} to it, keeping numeric order.
5. Run `npm run build-docs` to generate `doc/{rule_file}.md` and the `doc/Rules.md` entry (heading, Tags, Aliases, Parameters, body); if not generated, add them by hand following existing entries.
6. Ensure `doc/{rule_file}.md` exists (generated from doc-build).
   a new file in `doc/`, named like the 59 there that start with ``; shortest first: ReleaseProcess.md (21 lines), md039.md (22 lines), Prettier.md (28 lines), md018.md (28 lines), md019.md (29 lines), md020.md (30 lines)

## 2. Add rule to config schemas, samples and typings
Filled from your task: {rule_alias} = `no-duplicate-heading`, {tag} = `# Install`
Blanks: {rule_id} rule identifier such as MDnnn; {rule_description} the rule's description; {param} parameter name with type, bounds and default
1. Add a `case "{rule_id}":` in the rule switch of schema/build-config-schema.mjs defining the {param} property (description, type, minimum/maximum, default), following neighbouring cases. (only if the rule has parameters)
   `schema/build-config-schema.mjs:92-691` in for (const rule of rules) { › switch (ruleName) {
   ```
      92|   switch (ruleName) {
        ⋮
     685|         },
     686|         "default": []
     687|       };
     688|       break;
     689|     default:
     690|       break;
     691|   }
   ```
2. Add a `{rule_id}` entry (comment line `{rule_id}/no-duplicate-heading : {rule_description} : <doc url>` plus default parameters) to schema/.markdownlint.jsonc.
   `schema/.markdownlint.jsonc:2-363` in {
   ```
       2| {
        ⋮
     357|   "MD062": {
     358|     // Maximum number of lines (0 for no limit)
     359|     "maximum": 0,
     360|     // Fenced code languages to ignore
     361|     "ignore_languages": []
     362|   }
     363| }
   ```
3. Add the matching commented entry to schema/.markdownlint.yaml.
4. Add the rule to the typed interface in lib/configuration-strict.d.ts (JSDoc comment with the rule description + url, and the property with parameter types), and append {rule_id} to the # Install tag description list in that file.
5. Run `npm run build-config` to regenerate schema/markdownlint-config-schema.json and the strict schema (new rule property and {rule_id} appended to the # Install tag description). Verify both files contain the entry; add by hand if not generated.
   `schema/markdownlint-config-schema.json:6-5318` in { › "properties": {
   ```
       6|   "properties": {
        ⋮
    5312|             "warning"
    5313|           ]
    5314|         }
    5315|       ],
    5316|       "default": true
    5317|     }
    5318|   },
   ```
6. Check the strict schema also has the rule property and the updated tag description.
   `schema/markdownlint-config-schema-strict.json:6-5318` in { › "properties": {
   ```
       6|   "properties": {
        ⋮
    5312|             "warning"
    5313|           ]
    5314|         }
    5315|       ],
    5316|       "default": true
    5317|     }
    5318|   },
   ```

## Last: check it all with one command
When all your edits are in, run once: `npm run lint; npm run build-docs; npm run build-config; npm test`
These are the checks earlier runs of these workflows passed, in one call. Its output is long: keep its last 60 lines (`2>&1 | tail -n 60` in Bash, `2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 60` in PowerShell), or Claude Code saves it to a file you then have to read.
